labels.notes: A refactor with no paper label. Neither module docstring carries a ``**`label`**`` mark. SubArc.lean:62's bold `inextensible_nested ⇒ curve_nested` is a heading that was already there at HEAD, not a label. Lean = HEAD for every statement. I elaborated HEAD's two sources (git show HEAD:…SubArc.lean and HEAD:…PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean, concatenated under Causal.CurvesExtendSecondCountable, Causal.NestedCausalities and Causal.CauchyDual) and dumped every Causal.* constant of the two modules, internal ones included (matchers): name, kind, universe parameters, Expr.hash of type and of value, and the binder-info telescope. I compared that with the same dump of the current oleans of SubArc and PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy. The two dumps have the same constant set and agree in every field but one: the value hash of Extensible.of_top_tail (4167501621 → 1313063214). The six names keep their universes [u], their type hashes (2975726331, 1085155926, 866244712, 3189547148, 248471968, 3241684421) and their binder infos. The five moved lemmas and PastInextensible.of_retraction.match_1_1 keep their value hashes. These are exactly the closer's recorded figures, so the closer's before-record is confirmed independently. Byte identity: HEAD PIMC :92–202, :207–330, :332–347, :349–404 and :406–422 each occur once in the new SubArc and nowhere in the new PIMC. The last three ranges include their docstrings, so those three docstrings moved unchanged. Outside the module docstring, the new PIMC equals HEAD minus :87–423. Outside the module docstring, the new SubArc equals HEAD minus the old Extensible.of_top_tail (:182–284) plus the inserted blocks (:207–211, :212–489, :564–620, :740–763). Extensible.of_top_tail's four statement lines are byte-identical to HEAD :185–188 except `:= by` → `:=`. The new proof (:486–488) is `((extensible_iff ⟨t₁, ht₁⟩).1 hext).elim` into PastExtensible.of_top_tail …|>.extensible and FutureExtensible.of_top_tail …|>.extensible. Its used constants are extensible_iff, the two one-sided lemmas, the two .extensible read-backs and the definitions, and include neither pauseTop nor exists_compress. A mutation (Future → Past in the second branch) fails to elaborate. The pause is written once: outside comments, the only code occurrences of pauseTop or exists_compress in any Lean file of the hub (campaign probes aside) are SubArc § 1 (:116–143) and FutureExtensible.of_top_tail (:340–453). The two rewritten docstrings are accurate. PastExtensible.of_top_tail: for a past extension the image of φ must be a final segment of the new interval (StrictlyExtendsPast, Inextensible.lean:292–297), and the pause adds parameters in ]a + g(·), a + 1] above it. FutureExtensible.of_top_tail: pauseTop, exists_compress and the initial segment are what its proof does. The new docstring of Extensible.of_top_tail and the new SubArc/PIMC docstring sections are accurate too, and so are their line citations (SubArc :218, :335, :462, :510, :568, :684, :748; PIMC :108, :147, :162, :174, :182, :191, :198). The moved lemmas use only Causal.Causality, Causal.Inextensible and SubArc § 1 / one another (used-constant probe), so no import was needed, and none changed.

build.details: `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true` exits 0 with no output on Causal/CExtConnexeCauchy/SubArc.lean and Causal/PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean. On a /tmp copy of SubArc with #print axioms appended it also exits 0, and a /tmp mutant of the new proof fails, so the elaboration is real. `lake build --no-build` on the two edited modules and the six downstream ones reports 'All targets up-to-date (3181 jobs)'; no `lake build` was run. Under -DwarningAsError=true, Causal/CExtConnexeCauchy/Basic.lean, Causal/InextensibleNotLeNested.lean and Causal/BoundaryChartCauchy.lean each exit 0. The closer's Probe.lean reruns clean and prints the recorded checks, the 6 #check and 9 #print axioms lines, each [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], matching axioms.txt line for line. Its two mutation claims (a type hash +1; dropping the pauseTop guard) each make it fail, which I reran on /tmp copies. sorry/admit/axiom/native_decide: 0 in the code of both files and of Probe.lean (tools/ladder.py _code). The word sorry occurs only in each docstring's heading 'What is proved (no `sorry`)'.

checks.stale_olean_finding: Accurate. .lake/build/lib/lean/CausalScaffold/PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.{olean,ilean,trace,…} (2026-11-28 02:06) and .lake/build/ir/CausalScaffold/PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.* remain from before graduation, and scaffold/CausalScaffold/PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean does not exist. `lake env lean campaign/T-abs-past-inextensible-meets-cauchy/Probe.lean` fails at :1:0 with 'import CausalScaffold.PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy failed, environment already contains Causal.Causality.PastInextensible.of_retraction.match_1_1 from Causal.CExtConnexeCauchy.SubArc'. It affects no gate. lakefile.toml's CausalScaffold lib is `srcDir = "scaffold"`, `globs = ["CausalScaffold.*"]`, so Lake enumerates its modules from the source files and a sourceless olean is never a target. scaffold/CausalScaffold.lean does not import the name. `make -C lean-causal check` runs `lake build Causal`, `lake build CausalScaffold`, scripts/sorry_count.py and scripts/AxiomSweep.lean, which imports only the roots Causal and CausalScaffold, and no gate in tools/ replays campaign probes. So the stale olean is never imported by a gate. Whether to clean it: not needed, and not as part of this target. It is one of 110 sourceless CausalScaffold oleans left by earlier graduations, so the pattern is systemic. Deleting this one would only change the old probe's error ('unknown module' instead of 'already contains'). A blanket clean would break the replay of four other old probes that import graduated scaffold names and today run only through stale oleans: T-abs-flrw-type (CausalScaffold.FlrwType), T-abs-boundary-chart-cauchy, T-abs-ers-sc-witnesses and T-abs-inextensible-not-le-nested. If replayable probes matter, the fix is to retarget probes at strict names (the closer's kb_proposals[2]). Any .lake cleanup is the master's, since CAMPAIGN.md forbids a closer to touch .lake.

The keeper's commit 491b0a8b (05:31, before the REPORT was written at 05:39) shifted them. At HEAD they are :453, :4982–:4995 (PastInextensible.of_retraction (:353 …) is :4995) and :5011. findings.fix: Use the HEAD line numbers above when the stale prose is refreshed (journal / keeper pass). REPORT.json is the closer's record and need not be rewritten.

findings.what: 'This is the library's one pause construction' is true of the pauseTop reparametrisation: library-wide, pauseTop and exists_compress occur in code only in § 1 and in FutureExtensible.of_top_tail. But the library has another construction it calls a pause: Causal/InextensibleNestedBasics.lean:372, extensible_of_lt_two, 'after a pause at its last point', an ad-hoc constant piece with no pauseTop. Read literally, the sentence overreaches. Relatedly, SubArc.lean:98–99 says the two docstrings 'lost' the sentences on the former pause. They were rewritten (PastExtensible.of_top_tail's sentence now names FutureExtensible.of_top_tail's pause), not only removed.
findings.fix: Optional wording, e.g. 'This is the library's one pauseTop construction' (or 'the end-piece lemmas' one pause construction'), and 'were rewritten where they described Extensible.of_top_tail's former pause'.
